newsitem.title: UK: UK insurer assails Labour's medical insurance plan.
newsitem.headline: UK insurer assails Labour's medical insurance plan.

text.p: British private health insurer PPP on Wednesday assailed Labour's plans to withdraw tax relief for private medical insurance for people over the age of 60, saying it would increase hospital waiting lists and deprive the health service of income.

"Gordon Brown has turned a deaf ear to warnings from PPP healthcare, the industry, independent experts and his own advisors who have all demonstrated since the election that abolition of tax relief for medical insurance is both bad economics and disastrous for a cash-strapped NHS (National Health Service)..," the company said in a statement.

Delivering his first budget, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said the government would withdraw the tax relief which it estimated costs the Treasury 140 million pounds a year and which he said had failed to significantly raise the take-up of private medical insurance.

But PPP said the measure would take away valuable income from the health service. It estimated that income to the NHS from beds paid for by all people with private insurance amounted to more than 100 million pounds a year. Income from elderly people with private insurance was a lower figure, a spokesman said.
